title: Antique Sterling Silver Souvenir Spoon Washington DC Capitol New Library c1900
description_html:
Antique Sterling Silver Souvenir Spoon — The Capitol, Washington D.C. — circa 1897-1905

The bright-cut engraved bowl shows the U.S. Capitol Building with "THE CAPITOL / WASHINGTON D.C." lettering. The ornate multi-vignette handle carries "WASHINGTON D.C." down a twisted stem, an arch flanked by the Washington Monument, the "NEW LIBRARY," and the U.S. Treasury Building on the terminal.

The "New Library" vignette is the dating clue: the Library of Congress's Thomas Jefferson Building opened in 1897 and was known as the "new Library" for only its first several years — placing this spoon circa 1897-1905.

Details:

  • Sterling silver (.925), stamped STERLING with a small circular maker's trademark consistent with Watson & Newell Co. of Attleboro, Massachusetts (pre-1906 production).
  • Weighed at 14.88 grams on a digital scale; measures just over 5.5 inches.
  • No monogram.

Condition: bowl engraving crisp and bright with scattered light tarnish; handle relief sharp with dark patina in the crevices consistent with age. No dents, no bends, no repairs. Please review all photos, including the hallmark close-up.

Ships boxed with padding — never in a plain envelope — so it arrives exactly as pictured.

A handsome turn-of-the-century piece for collectors of Washington D.C. memorabilia, Library of Congress history, or antique American souvenir spoons.
